exclusions: general code debugging outside agent layers
security scanning of agent boundaries
agent performance benchmarking
writing new agent features
preconditions: an agent or LLM application exists to audit
logs, configs, or source for the failing agent behavior are reachable

exclusions: debugging a specific failing agent run
security hardening of agent trust boundaries
auditing an existing agent stack layer by layer
preconditions: an agent loop or tool-calling surface exists or is being designed
ability to change tool definitions and observation formats

exclusions: verifying a feature after code changes
framework-specific bugs with a narrower skill
root-cause analysis of a whole agent stack's design
preconditions: an agent run is failing, looping, or burning tokens without progress
the failing run's tool history and logs are available

exclusions: general web application authentication and injection review
repository-wide automated vulnerability scanning
penetration testing or exploit development
host, container, or cloud infrastructure hardening
preconditions: an agent runtime, tool gateway, or memory service to review
tests can exercise the real action entry point

exclusions: writing a generic HTTP client with no repo integration pattern
designing a brand new public API from scratch
frontend UI work that only consumes an existing connector
preconditions: the host repo already has at least two integration examples
the target API's auth model and endpoints are known

exclusions: no reproducible benchmark or baseline is available
no automated correctness gate protects the behavior
subjective quality improvements that no metric captures
preconditions: the operation to optimize is runnable on demand
a measurable metric and a correctness gate both exist

exclusions: auditing code quality or security of a known codebase
implementing features in a repo you already understand
deep design review of a single module
preconditions: read access to an unfamiliar repository
project manifests, CI config, and tests are present

exclusions: React composition, hooks, or rendering architecture
backend service layering and API design details
framework-specific patterns covered by a dedicated skill
preconditions: no narrower framework-specific skill applies
code to review or conventions to establish

exclusions: data that must always be fresh, such as real-time feeds
cache entries too large to store as files
results that depend on parameters beyond file content
preconditions: the same expensive file processing runs repeatedly
processing logic can be kept as a pure function to wrap

exclusions: a single-module boundary changed in one atomic commit
choosing resource and error semantics for a new API
writing regression tests for previously fixed bugs
preconditions: two or more independently owned consumers of a boundary
a version-controlled contract artifact can be authored

exclusions: local model inference with no per-call API spend
prompt quality tuning with no cost constraint
a single one-off LLM call
preconditions: the application calls a hosted LLM API
a spend budget or cost target is defined

exclusions: questions answerable from the local repository alone
environments without Context7 or network access
general programming concepts not tied to a library
preconditions: the Context7 MCP server is configured
the question depends on a named library, framework, or API

exclusions: unit testing ordinary application code
one-off manual QA of a single output
benchmarking raw model latency or throughput
preconditions: a task or capability with definable pass/fail criteria
evals can be run repeatedly against the agent

exclusions: Trivial changes such as typo fixes or single-line config tweaks
Diary-style narration of events without a transferable pattern
Tasks where no retrospective capture was requested
preconditions: A completed task, debugging session, failure, or rollback worth reflecting on
Access to the notes store where growth entries are kept

exclusions: Throwaway scripts with no domain logic
Big-bang rewrites of the whole service
Framework-only changes that never touch application boundaries
preconditions: A service whose domain logic is entangled with I/O or framework code
Room to introduce ports and adapters slice by slice rather than by rewrite

exclusions: Greenfield projects with no established conventions
Judging syntax or tech-stack quality
Reformatting existing code instead of codifying its style
Extracting implicit rules from a single file
preconditions: Read and write access to the project root
Git history for incremental diff mode, or file timestamps as a fallback

exclusions: Trivial edits or one-line fixes
Active debugging sessions
Code review requests
Implementation whose acceptance conditions are already clear
preconditions: A feature or change whose expected outcome is ambiguous or high-impact
Repository, docs, or issue context available for local fact-finding

exclusions: Context that is already fully known upfront
Single-file questions that need no retrieval loop
Replacing a production vector-search pipeline
preconditions: A subagent or agent workflow that receives limited context
Ability to run repeated search and retrieval passes

exclusions: Batch or offline workloads with no latency requirement
Trading or financial advice
Dropping required validation to gain speed
Unapproved production deploys, live orders, or destructive migrations
preconditions: A latency-sensitive surface such as a dashboard, feed, queue, or gateway
Ability to measure p50/p95/p99 and freshness in the target environment

exclusions: Executing or starting discovered MCP servers
Confirming compromise or a vulnerability from mutability alone
Home-directory or machine-wide config unless explicitly requested
A full MCP security assessment
preconditions: A repo-scoped MCP configuration file to inspect
Permission to read configuration as text without executing it

exclusions: Choosing whether a capability should be a rule, skill, MCP, or CLI
Static review of existing MCP configuration
Non-MCP REST or GraphQL API design
preconditions: A Node or TypeScript project that will host the MCP server
Current MCP SDK docs or Context7 access to confirm signatures

exclusions: Formal legal, financial, or regulatory compliance audits
Pure libraries or docs-only repos unless release packaging is the question
Line-level secure coding during active implementation
A product idea with no repo, deployment, or runtime surface
preconditions: A repository, release branch, PR, or deployed URL to inspect
Authorization to gather local evidence without external uploads

exclusions: Improving a single prompt's quality (use prompt-optimizer)
General application, CDN, or database caching
Claiming measured savings without provider counters
Unauthorized provider traffic or invoice access
preconditions: Repeated LLM API requests that share instructions, tools, or reference material
Exact provider endpoint, model, service tier, and caching mode identified

exclusions: Executing the task the prompt describes
Optimizing code or runtime performance
ECC configuration changes (use configure-ecc)
Skill inventory questions (use skill-stocktake)
preconditions: A draft prompt the user wants critiqued or rewritten
Advisory-only intent: the user is not asking for execution

exclusions: Free-form, highly variable text with no stable pattern
Sending all content to an LLM when regex covers most cases
Mutating parsed items in place during validation
preconditions: Structured text with repeating patterns to extract
A way to measure regex success and flag low-confidence items

exclusions: Running the audit before the external skill is installed and the harness reloaded
Small single-stack projects needing only a file count
Vulnerability or dependency-CVE scanning
Audits that would send repository contents to third parties
preconditions: A large legacy or monorepo codebase needing a structural inventory
Permission to clone and install the pinned external skill

exclusions: purely conceptual question that needs no external evidence
preconditions: a concrete feature or dependency decision to research before coding
a diff, module, or endpoint surface to review
a test runner that can execute the project's suite
